diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, since we set $Q(0)=1$, there is uncertainty only on $B(0)$ and then the direction of perturbation is $\widehat{z}_0=(0,\pm 1)$ (in any vector $p$-norm).

issues.failure_explanation: In the swapped convention of the remark ($y_0=(1,0.60)$ available, $\widetilde y_0=(1,0.61)$ actual), the perturbation direction is still $\widehat z_0=(0,\pm1)$, so the paper's own formula (expression) gives $K_\infty(y_0,\widehat z_0)=\sqrt{1+0.60^2}/\vert-1+0.60\vert=1.1662/0.4\approx2.92$, not $2.29$. The value $2.29$ is inconsistent with (expression), while the companion value $3.00$ quoted for $B(0)=0.61$ is correctly given by (expression) ($\sqrt{1.3721}/0.39\approx3.00$), confirming the formula and the wrongness of $2.29$.

failure_location.quote: In the case of the GDP-ND model, we have $K_\infty(y_0,\widehat{z}_0)=2.29$ for $B(0)=0.60$, instead of $K_\infty(y_0,\widehat{z}_0)=3.00$ for $B(0)=0.61$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $2.29$ by the value $\approx2.92$ forced by (expression) for $B(0)=0.60$ with $w^{(1)}_1/w^{(1)}_2=-1$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the numerical value in this remark is wrong; the remark's interpretive conclusion (a computable asymptotic condition number under the swapped convention) and all formal results, including (expression) and Theorem thm:added-1, are unaffected.
issues.title: Incorrect value K_infty = 2.29 for B(0)=0.60 in the GDP-ND swapped-convention remark
issues.why_classification: A single wrong numerical value in an illustrative remark; the correct value follows directly from the paper's own displayed formula, and the remark's point and all downstream claims survive the one-line correction, so nothing substantive is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Euclidean norm as vector norm, we have $V_1=0.9988$ and $W_1=0.9986$.

issues.failure_explanation: The $V_1$-dependent term of (epsilonc<) is $\frac{1}{(r_1-r_2)\widehat t}\cdot\frac12\log\frac{1}{1-V_1}$, which for $V_1=0.9988$ equals $\frac12\log\frac{1}{0.0012}\approx3.36$; the example instead displays $\frac12\log\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-V_1}}=1.6844$ (an extra square root, i.e. half the correct term), so the value shown is not the term appearing in (epsilonc<). A direct derivation for this example (precision $\bar\epsilon$ requires $e^{-t}\cdot0.0601\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-V_1}}\leq\frac{\bar\epsilon}{2+\bar\epsilon}$, i.e. $t\geq\log2+\frac12\log\frac1{1-V_1}+\log0.0601+\log\frac{2+\bar\epsilon}{\bar\epsilon}\approx1.24+\log\frac{2+\bar\epsilon}{\bar\epsilon}$) confirms the correct term is $\frac12\log\frac1{1-V_1}$.

failure_location.quote: and in (\ref{epsilonc<}) we have $$\frac{1}{(r_1-r_2)\widehat{t}}\log\frac{f_2}{f_1}=-2.8115\text{\ \ and\ \ }\frac{1}{(r_1-r_2)\widehat{t}}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-V_1}}=1.6844$$ using $\widehat{t}=1$ as time unit.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-V_1}}$ by $\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{1-V_1}$ (value $\approx3.36$) in the example's evaluation of (epsilonc<).
issues.overall_effect: Only the numerical evaluation of the onset speed in this example is wrong; the bound (epsilonc<) itself and the paper's onset analysis are unaffected, and the example's qualitative conclusion (the asymptotic behavior is quickly attained) survives with the corrected term.
issues.title: Example 7.6 mis-evaluates the V_1 term of the onset bound (epsilonc<): 1.6844 instead of about 3.36
issues.why_classification: A contained, local correction of one evaluated term in a numerical illustration; the example's conclusion of a quickly attained asymptotic behavior is unchanged, so no rate, regime, or guarantee is lost.
